purpose: How a small business-email and cloud-subscription reseller runs a client account after it is live: how seats, licence terms and invoices are reconciled every cycle so neither party pays for what it does not use, how administrative access is held and re-attested as a fiduciary-grade duty, what the recurring fee actually buys and where support stops, how a recurring security-posture review turns an invisible subscription into a service worth renewing, how renewals and supplier price changes are disclosed rather than sprung, when an add-on may honestly be proposed and on what tenant-specific evidence, and how the operator sees churn coming and hands an account back cleanly when the relationship ends.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is a solo or very small shop holding a book of small-business tenants that were sold under the reseller-programs KB and built and migrated under the tenant-setup KB; this KB begins at the accepted handover of a live environment

the recurring leg has two parts, a pass-through subscription carrying a spread and a management fee for the operator's own labour, and the book only compounds if accounts survive the first and second renewal

every price, buy rate, spread, seat threshold, cancellation or adjustment window, retention duration, response target and churn figure in this KB is a mechanism to be re-pulled from a dated provider price list, the current program terms or the operator's own measured records, never recalled from memory or quoted as a market fact

partner-program terms, licence family composition, delegated-administration mechanics, native retention behaviour and admin role catalogues are vendor-controlled and are restructured periodically without the operator's input; every statement about them is a dated snapshot to be re-verified

the operator's and the client's jurisdictions govern data protection, breach notification, employee-monitoring limits, recurring-billing disclosure and indirect tax on resold subscriptions; this KB names the obligation class and directs both parties to verify current rules in their own jurisdiction with their own advisers, and is not legal, tax, accounting or insurance advice
administrative access to a client tenant is held on the client's behalf under a documented authorization and least privilege, and every privileged action is logged
exclusions: how indirect-reseller and partner programs are structured, who bills whom, where the per-seat spread comes from, which suite to anchor the practice on, which small-business segments to pursue, the trusted-operator positioning and the sale-time right-sizing and pricing of the offer, all of which belong to the cloud-reseller-programs-and-SMB-targeting KB; this KB starts after a disclosed offer has been signed and an authorization exists

tenant architecture and the delivered security baseline, multi-factor and administrator-separation design, mail and data migration planning, cutover execution, DNS and domain-record integrity, first user onboarding and training, and authoring the documentation of the delivered environment, all of which belong to the tenant-setup-migration-and-onboarding KB; this KB accepts that documentation at handover and maintains it thereafter

invented specifics of any kind: no per-seat price, spread percentage, discount, cancellation-window length, retention-window duration, response-time commitment, ticket volume, attach rate, churn rate or account multiple is asserted as fact here, because each is a mechanism to derive from a dated source or from the operator's own records

fear-based upselling in every form: breach anecdotes, borrowed statistics, implied liability, manufactured urgency, vendor-quota or attach-rate campaigns, and any add-on, tier or seat recommended without a dated observation in that specific tenant showing the need

holding standing global administrative rights for convenience, sharing one administrative credential across clients, acting on the instruction of someone with no authority to give it, or opening mailbox contents outside a specific written authorization

personalized legal, tax, accounting, insurance or compliance advice to the operator or the client; obligation classes are named, written instruction is required before acting, and both parties verify current rules in their jurisdiction with their own advisers; no compliance outcome is ever promised

promising uptime, deliverability, threat-prevention or data-recovery outcomes beyond what the vendor's published terms provide and the operator can itself control, and stating any avoided-loss, return-on-investment or benchmark figure in an account review that cannot be traced to a line in that client's own history

enterprise account management, multi-tenant consolidation, around-the-clock monitoring or security-operations-centre services, forensic investigation and attribution, and the hiring and management of a support team, all outside the small-shop frame this KB assumes

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RECURRING_BOOK_THESIS states the cadence, the unit of account, what the recurring fee buys and what the book is not, and ACCOUNT_SERVICE_RECORD enumerates the per-tenant fields, the change log and who may request a change

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: STANDING_ACCESS_STEWARDSHIP defines least-privilege role scoping, just-in-time elevation, the access register, the re-attestation cadence and triggers, the privileged-action log and the revocation path, and states that delegation mechanics are vendor-controlled and must be re-verified

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NEED_EVIDENCE_STANDARD requires a dated tenant-specific observation, a stated do-nothing option and disclosure of the operator's interest while banning borrowed statistics and quota campaigns, and EXPANSION_CATALOG_FIT states for each service the failure it addresses, what it does not cover, the licence overlap to check first and the capability test the operator must pass before selling it

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RENEWAL_AND_REPRICING_CYCLE works backwards from the anniversary through the notice window with a pre-renewal reconciliation and a written statement separating supplier changes from the operator's own fee, and CHURN_SIGNAL_WATCH lists the leading signals with a conversation-shaped response and the honest decision to let some accounts go

competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ACCOUNT_REVIEW_VALUE_EVIDENCE builds a one-page review sourced only from the operator's own records including declined risks and what was not covered, and OFFBOARDING_EXIT_INTEGRITY hands over tenant ownership, transfers or releases subscriptions, removes access with written confirmation and settles billing without withholding anything as leverage

glossary.definition: The two directions of a subscription-quantity change: a true-up adds paid seats to match people who are actually working, a true-down removes seats that no longer have a user. True-ups are usually provisionable immediately; true-downs are constrained by the commitment term and by an adjustment window whose existence, length and behaviour are program-defined and periodically revised, so both must be checked against current terms rather than remembered.

The gap that opens between three counts that ought to match: licences assigned inside the tenant, subscription quantity being paid for, and people actually doing work. Drift accumulates from hires, departures, role changes, trials, duplicate accounts and licences attached to objects that are not people, and it costs the client money in one direction and the operator money in the other.

A mailbox or directory object that represents something other than a person, such as a shared mailbox, a room or equipment resource, a distribution list, an alias on an existing mailbox, or a service account used by an application. Several of these classes do not require a paid seat in typical configurations, but the rules are vendor-defined and vary by suite and tier, so each is checked against current documentation rather than assumed.

Two separate axes of a subscription that are often confused: the term is how long the quantity is committed for, the billing frequency is how often it is invoiced. A subscription can be committed for a long term but billed in short cycles, which feels flexible while the quantity is in fact locked. The available combinations, their price differences and their reduction rules are program-controlled and dated.

The mechanism class by which a partner administers a customer's tenant without holding an account inside it, granted by the customer, scoped to specific administrative roles and, in current models, time-bound and subject to renewal. The specific framework, the role catalogue and the expiry behaviour are vendor-controlled and have been restructured more than once; verify the current model before relying on any detail of it.

A repeatable, scheduled inspection of a delivered tenant against the security baseline it was built to, producing a dated findings list with severity, a recommended fix, an owner, and an explicit record where the client declines. It is a judgement exercise about which findings matter in this particular business, not a scan report, and it is the main recurring artifact that makes a subscription feel like a service.

The division between what a cloud suite vendor is responsible for, broadly the availability and integrity of the platform, and what remains the customer's responsibility, broadly the content of their data, who has access to it, and the consequences of their own deletions and configuration. Where the line falls for a given service is set by the vendor's published terms; it is stated to clients from those terms, never from a sales narrative about what the vendor supposedly does not do.

Two different things a client can mean by asking whether their mail is backed up. Native retention means the recovery behaviour the suite itself provides, such as deleted-item recovery, retention policies and recoverable-item windows, all of which have vendor-defined durations and limits. A third-party backup is a separate copy under a separate control plane, sold for restore granularity, retention beyond the native window, departed-user data and protection against deletions made inside the tenant. The honest comparison names both, with the native behaviour verified in current documentation.

glossary.term: cost to serve and contribution per account-month
glossary.definition: The operator's measurement of what one account actually consumes in a month, in support minutes, out-of-scope minutes, administrative minutes and incident time, set against what the account actually contributes, being the verified subscription spread plus the management fee net of payment and platform costs. The pair produces a contribution per account-month and a floor below which an account should not be accepted or retained; both come from the operator's own records, not from any industry figure.

The period before an anniversary in which a quantity or term can still be changed, and the period after an order in which an adjustment or cancellation is permitted. Both are program-defined mechanisms whose existence and length vary by suite, term class and region and are periodically revised; the operator holds them per subscription in a dated register and works backwards from the anniversary so that a client's right to reduce is exercisable rather than theoretical.

nodes.definition: State plainly what the book of live tenants is and how it will be operated, because a subscription book that is treated as passive residual income decays quietly. Fix the operating rhythm: a monthly cycle in which every tenant's seats and invoices are reconciled, a periodic security-posture review, an annual renewal worked backwards from each anniversary, and an account review that puts the invisible work in front of the client. Fix the unit of account as the account-month, because every later measurement, price and exit decision is expressed per account per month. Separate the two revenue legs and decide explicitly which one funds labour: a pass-through subscription carrying a spread scales with seats but not with effort, while a management fee is what actually pays for the hours, and a book priced entirely on the spread quietly funds unlimited support from a fixed margin. Name what the book is not, in writing, so the boundary is a decision rather than a mood: not a general helpdesk for anything with a screen, not the client's IT department, not a guarantee of outcomes the vendor itself does not guarantee. Finally, tie growth to capacity: the book may only grow as fast as the rhythm can absorb, because the failure mode of this business is not too few clients, it is more accounts than cycles.

included: the operating cadence and what happens in each cycle
the account-month as the unit of account
which revenue leg funds labour
the written list of what the book does not do
the capacity limit on book growth
excluded: how the offer was priced, disclosed and sold in the first place, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
the build and migration of the environment, which belongs to the tenant-setup KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cycle is missed across several tenants, or measured labour shows the spread rather than the management fee is funding support hours

pros.claim: A stated rhythm converts a book of accounts into a schedule that a solo operator can actually execute, instead of a queue of interruptions
pros.example: knowing on the first working day of the month exactly which tenants get reconciled, which are due a posture review, and which anniversaries fall inside the next notice window

pros.claim: Deciding up front that the management fee funds labour keeps the spread from silently subsidising unbounded support
pros.example: an account whose seat count halves after layoffs still paying for the same administrative hours because the fee never depended on the seat count

cons.claim: A uniform rhythm spends real hours on accounts that generate almost no work, and the smallest tenants are exactly the ones least able to pay for those hours
cons.example: a five-person firm with no staff changes for a year still consuming a monthly reconciliation slot and a quarterly review

cons.claim: Writing down what the book is not creates conversations the operator would rather avoid and can cost a deal that was already half-sold
cons.example: telling an owner during handover that their point-of-sale terminal and their accounting package are outside the service they just bought

failure_modes: treating the recurring line as passive income and touching a tenant only when it breaks
pricing the whole relationship on the seat spread so that every additional support hour destroys the margin it was supposed to earn
adding accounts faster than the cycle can absorb until reconciliation and reviews quietly stop happening
leaving the boundary implicit so each client invents their own idea of what the fee covers
acceptance_tests: the rhythm names every recurring activity, its cadence and the tenant set it applies to, and a calendar exists that a stand-in could execute
the document states which revenue leg funds labour and lists at least three things the book explicitly does not do
revisit_triggers: the book grows past the point where a full cycle can be completed in the time available
a repeated support pattern shows the fee structure is funding work it was never meant to fund
a change in the transacting route alters which revenue leg the operator actually controls

nodes.definition: Maintain one record per tenant that makes management possible when the operator touches that environment once every few weeks and remembers nothing. It carries the tenant identifier and the accepted handover documentation from the build, the subscription inventory with licence family, quantity, term class, billing frequency and anniversary for each line, the assigned-licence baseline from the last reconciliation, the named authorized signer and the list of people who may request a change or raise a ticket, the authorization scope and its expiry, escalation and after-hours contacts, the domain and DNS custodianship position, third-party applications and integrations that touch mail or identity, backup and retention configuration as actually deployed, and a dated change log of every action the operator has taken. The record is not documentation for its own sake: it is the artifact every other work unit in this KB reads from and writes back to, and its quality decides whether a reconciliation takes twenty minutes or half a day. Keep it where a stand-in could use it during illness or holiday, review it on the same cadence as the reconciliation, and treat a field the operator cannot evidence as unknown rather than assumed, because an assumed anniversary or an assumed authorized requester is how a renewal is missed or an unauthorized change is made.

included: the field set per tenant
the dated change log
the authorized-requester and signer list with authorization scope and expiry
the review cadence of the record itself
the explicit marking of unknown fields
excluded: authoring the as-built environment documentation, which the tenant-setup KB produces and hands over
the sales and qualification file that preceded the signed offer
the client's own internal staff records beyond who may request what

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a reconciliation or renewal reveals a field the record asserted incorrectly, or a stand-in cannot complete a routine task from the record alone

pros.claim: A single per-tenant record removes the recall problem that makes small-book management error-prone, and makes the operator substitutable during absence
pros.example: a stand-in handling a leaver request correctly because the record names the authorized signer, the retention position and where the shared mailboxes sit

pros.claim: A dated change log converts disputes into lookups, both with clients and with the provider
pros.example: answering an invoice query about three seats added in the middle of a cycle by showing the request, the date and the person who asked

cons.claim: The record only stays true if it is written back to during the work, and a record that is trusted while stale is more dangerous than none
cons.example: a licence reclaimed during a busy week and never logged, so the next reconciliation chases a variance the operator created itself

cons.claim: It concentrates sensitive material about a client's environment in one place, which raises the operator's own security obligations
cons.example: an unencrypted record listing administrative contacts, integrations and domain custodianship for a dozen small businesses

failure_modes: keeping the record in the operator's head and in scattered emails
copying the build documentation once and never updating it as the environment changes
recording a subscription without its term class or anniversary, so nothing downstream can say what may change today
listing an authorized requester who has since left the client
acceptance_tests: every live tenant has a record with subscription lines, term classes, anniversaries, authorized signer and requesters, authorization scope and expiry, and escalation contacts populated or explicitly marked unknown
the last three changes made in any tenant appear in the change log with date, requester and what was done
revisit_triggers: a handover is accepted from the build phase for a new tenant
the client changes owner, signer, office manager or accountant
a reconciliation finds a field that the record asserted and the tenant contradicts

nodes.definition: Hold administrative access to client tenants the way a professional holds keys to someone else's premises, for the whole life of the relationship rather than only at the moment it is granted. Assign the least privileged role that accomplishes the task rather than a global administrator role kept for convenience; give each person at the operator their own identity with their own multi-factor enrolment instead of a shared credential; elevate for a task and step back down; keep an access register naming every tenant the operator can reach, by which mechanism, in which role, under which authorization and until when, and reconcile that register against the provider portal on a cadence rather than trusting it. Re-attest access on a schedule and on every trigger: a change of the operator's staff, a change of the client's signer or owner, a change in the vendor's delegation model, and the end of any temporary elevation. Log every privileged action with what was done, when, why and under whose authorization, because that log is the only thing that distinguishes stewardship from access in retrospect. When a request arrives from someone not on the authorized list, the answer is to pause and confirm with the signer, not to be helpful. The mechanics of partner delegation are vendor-controlled and have been restructured more than once; treat any specific detail as a dated snapshot to re-verify.

included: least-privilege role scoping and just-in-time elevation
per-person operator identities with their own second factor
the access register and its reconciliation to the provider portal
re-attestation cadence and triggers
the privileged-action log
revocation on departure at either party
excluded: the original authorization negotiated and signed at the point of sale, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
the tenant's own administrator architecture and break-glass design as built, which belongs to the tenant-setup KB
forensic investigation of misuse, which is beyond the small-shop frame

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vendor change to the delegation framework, a staffing change at either party, or a review that finds access the register did not know about

pros.claim: Least privilege plus a log turns the operator's riskiest asset into its most defensible one, and is the only honest answer when a client asks what the operator can see
pros.example: showing an owner a register entry stating exactly which administrative role the operator holds in their tenant, under which authorization, with an expiry date

pros.claim: Re-attestation catches the access nobody would have thought to remove, which is where the real exposure sits
pros.example: a scheduled review finding an active administrative relationship with a client who ended the engagement a year earlier

cons.claim: Scoped, expiring access costs time on every job and occasionally blocks the operator at the worst moment, which is a real and recurring temptation to keep standing rights
cons.example: needing an elevation approved by an owner who is on a flight while a mail-flow problem is live

cons.claim: The mechanics are vendor-controlled, so an access model that is correct today can be deprecated on the vendor's schedule and force a re-mapping across the whole book
cons.example: a delegation framework change that requires every client relationship to be re-established with newly scoped roles inside a fixed window

failure_modes: holding standing global administrator rights across the book because it is faster
sharing one administrative credential among the operator's people so no action can be attributed
acting on a plausible request from an unauthorized person because they were confident and in a hurry
letting delegated access outlive the engagement that justified it
opening mailbox contents on a verbal request without a written, scoped authorization
acceptance_tests: no tenant carries standing global administrative rights except under a named, dated exception with a stated expiry and a reason
the access register reconciles to what the provider portal actually shows, with no unexplained relationships in either direction
every privileged action in the last cycle has a log entry naming the action, the time, the reason and the authorization it relied on
access removal after an engagement ends is evidenced by a confirmation record, not by memory
revisit_triggers: the vendor changes its delegated-administration model, role catalogue or expiry behaviour
anyone joins or leaves the operator
the client's authorized signer or ownership changes
any temporary elevation passes its stated expiry

nodes.definition: Hold, per subscription and per tenant, the structure that decides what may be changed and when, because almost every seat conversation is really a term conversation. Record the term class the subscription sits on, the billing frequency as a separate axis from the term, the anniversary date, whether an adjustment or cancellation window applies and what it does, whether mid-term reductions are possible at all, whether promotional pricing has an expiry, and how the tenant's several subscriptions align or fail to align with each other. Every one of these is program-defined, differs by suite and region, and is revised on the vendor's schedule, so each entry carries the date it was checked and the source it came from, and anything unverified is marked unknown rather than assumed. Alignment is a decision the operator should make deliberately: subscriptions with scattered anniversaries mean a renewal conversation every few weeks and no clean moment to reduce, while consolidating anniversaries makes the account governable but concentrates the client's exposure to a single renewal event. The register exists so that no promise about adding, removing or re-pricing a seat is ever made from memory, and so that the client's right to reduce is exercisable on a date the operator already knows.

included: term class and billing frequency per subscription
anniversary and window dates with the date checked and the source
mid-term reduction rules as currently documented
promotional expiry tracking
anniversary alignment decisions across a tenant
excluded: the choice of term made at the original sale and how it was priced, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
the program topology and who bills whom
negotiating program terms with a provider

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published program change to terms, windows or reduction rules, or a provider response that contradicts a register entry

pros.claim: A dated register makes every seat answer instant and defensible, and stops the operator promising a reduction the term does not permit
pros.example: answering a client who wants to drop four seats in the middle of a term with the exact date those reductions become actionable, in the same conversation

pros.claim: Deliberate anniversary alignment turns a scattered account into one governable renewal event with a real window in which to act
pros.example: consolidating three subscriptions bought at different times so the pre-renewal reconciliation happens once rather than three times a year

cons.claim: The register is only as good as its last check, and the underlying rules change without the operator being told in a way they will notice
cons.example: a window rule the operator quoted confidently having been revised two program updates earlier

cons.claim: Alignment work can itself require accepting a term change or a co-terminated period that costs the client money in the short run
cons.example: a shortened bridging period on one subscription to bring it onto the same anniversary as the others

failure_modes: quoting a cancellation or adjustment window from memory or from a competitor's blog post
recording an anniversary without recording the term class, so nothing can be said about reductions
treating billing frequency as if it were the commitment term and promising flexibility that does not exist
letting a promotional price expire silently into a renewal statement
acceptance_tests: every live subscription line has a term class, a billing frequency, an anniversary, a source and the date it was last checked
any window or reduction rule stated to a client can be traced to a dated entry, and unverified rules are marked unknown rather than presented as fact
revisit_triggers: the vendor or provider publishes a change to term classes, windows or reduction rules
a subscription is added, renewed or re-termed in any tenant
a promotional price approaches its expiry

nodes.definition: Every cycle, compare three counts that always drift apart and are never checked by anyone else: licences actually assigned inside the tenant, subscription quantity the client is actually paying for, and people actually doing work at the client. Pull the assigned-licence list, obtain the current staff position from the person who genuinely knows it, usually the owner, office manager or whoever runs payroll, and classify every difference rather than just totalling it. The classes matter because each has a different action: paid but unassigned, which is the client's money going nowhere; assigned to someone who has left, which is both waste and an access exposure; licences attached to objects that are not people, where the shared mailbox, resource, alias and service-account rules must be checked against current vendor documentation rather than assumed; contractors and seasonal staff who legitimately come and go; duplicate or test accounts left from the migration; and people working without the entitlement they need, which is the honest true-up the client will thank the operator for. Output a dated variance list where every line has a classification, an action and an owner. Make finding money for the client an explicit purpose of the exercise: a reconciliation whose output only ever adds seats will eventually be recognised for what it is, and the credibility lost is worth far more than the seats gained.

included: the three-way count and its sources
classification of every difference
the dated variance list with actions and owners
the cadence and who at the client supplies the staff position
excluded: executing the resulting changes, which is the true-up and true-down unit
the licence mix decided at the original sale
the mailbox and group architecture created during migration

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cycle in which the variance list is materially larger or smaller than usual, or vendor guidance that changes how a licence class must be counted

pros.claim: The exercise regularly finds money for the client, which is the cheapest and most durable retention asset the operator has
pros.example: a reconciliation that surfaces several paid-but-unassigned seats left over from a seasonal peak, returned to the client as a reduction they did not ask for

pros.claim: It catches access exposure that no other routine catches, because a licence assigned to a departed person usually means an account that still works
pros.example: finding an active mailbox for someone who left months earlier, still receiving mail and still able to sign in

cons.claim: It depends on a staff list the client may not maintain accurately, which puts the operator in the position of asking uncomfortable questions every cycle
cons.example: an owner who cannot say without checking whether a part-time bookkeeper is still engaged

cons.claim: Honest reconciliation reduces the operator's own recurring revenue in a way no client will ever audit, so the discipline is entirely self-imposed
cons.example: reporting unassigned seats that would have gone on being billed indefinitely without anyone noticing

failure_modes: comparing only two of the three counts and calling it a reconciliation
treating every non-human object as if it needed a paid seat, or assuming it never does, instead of checking the current rules
producing a variance list with no owner and no date, so nothing is executed
running the reconciliation only when the client complains about an invoice
acceptance_tests: each cycle produces a dated variance list in which every difference carries a classification, an action and a named owner
the staff position used in the comparison is attributed to a named person at the client and dated
at least the paid-but-unassigned and assigned-to-departed classes are reported to the client whether or not they reduce the invoice
revisit_triggers: the client reports a hiring round, redundancies, a seasonal peak or an acquisition
a variance class recurs for three cycles, which means a process at the client is generating it
vendor documentation changes what a non-human object requires

nodes.definition: Turn the variance list into subscription changes without destroying anything or promising what the term forbids. For each line decide which of four things applies: provision now, because an addition is almost always immediately available and someone is working without what they need; reduce now, if the current term and window genuinely permit it today; queue the reduction with the date it becomes actionable, which is the discipline that separates a managed book from a billing service; or leave it deliberately, with the reason recorded. Every executed change needs a written request trail from an authorized requester, an effective date, and a verification step after the change, because provisioning that silently half-completes is common enough to plan for. Reductions demand more care than additions, since removing a licence can begin the clock on data the client still needs, and an unlicensed mailbox does not behave like a licensed one; the retention decision must already be recorded before a seat is reclaimed. Hold the pending-reduction queue as a live artifact with dates, review it every cycle, and execute it without waiting to be reminded: a client who discovers that a reduction they asked for six months ago was never actioned at its window has learned something about the operator that no apology fixes.

included: the four dispositions for a variance line
the pending-reduction queue with actionable dates
written request trail, effective dates and post-change verification
the ordering rule that retention decisions precede reclaim
excluded: the term rules themselves, which the term register holds
checking the resulting invoice, which is the billing reconciliation unit
the data-retention decision itself, which the client makes and the leaver runbook captures

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vendor change to what licence removal does to mailbox data, or an executed change that produced an outcome the operator did not expect

pros.claim: A dated pending-reduction queue is the single feature that makes a client believe the operator is on their side, because it costs the operator money on a schedule
pros.example: a reduction requested mid-term being executed automatically on the day the window opens, with the client told before they noticed the date

pros.claim: Post-change verification catches the partial provisioning that otherwise surfaces as a support ticket from a new hire on their first morning
pros.example: confirming that an assigned licence actually resulted in a working mailbox and enrolled second factor before the start date

cons.claim: Reductions are the irreversible direction: reclaiming a licence can start a deletion clock on data that has no other copy, and the recovery window is vendor-defined and short
cons.example: a mailbox reclaimed before the owner's tax adviser had finished with three years of correspondence

cons.claim: Maintaining a queue of future actions imposes a memory burden that a busy solo operator will drop first when a cycle gets compressed
cons.example: a queued reduction whose window passes during a fortnight dominated by one client's migration problem

failure_modes: reclaiming a licence before the client's retention decision is recorded
telling a client a reduction is impossible when it is merely not possible today
executing a change on a verbal request from someone not on the authorized list
letting the queue rot until the windows pass
assuming a provisioning action completed because the portal accepted it
acceptance_tests: every executed change has a written request from an authorized requester, an effective date and a recorded verification result
every blocked reduction sits in the queue with the date it becomes actionable and the term entry that blocks it
no licence reclaim appears in the log without a prior recorded retention decision for that user's data
revisit_triggers: a queued reduction's window is missed for any reason
a vendor change alters what happens to data when a licence is removed
a provisioning action fails verification more than occasionally

nodes.definition: Write and follow the three per-person paths that generate most of the routine work in a small tenant, because each of them done ad hoc leaves residue that surfaces months later as a variance, an exposure or an angry phone call. Joiner: create the account to a standard naming and attribute convention, assign the entitlement the role actually needs from the pool before buying anything new, enrol the second factor, add group, distribution and shared-mailbox memberships from the role definition rather than by copying a colleague's account wholesale, enrol the device if devices are managed, and hand over to the client's own induction with a short written note of what the person now has. Mover: change entitlements to the new role and, critically, remove the old delegations, shared-mailbox rights and group memberships instead of letting them accumulate, since long-serving staff otherwise quietly acquire access to everything. Leaver: run the sequence that actually protects the business, in order — revoke sessions and reset credentials, remove second-factor methods and device access, capture the client's written decision on the mailbox and its data, convert to a shared mailbox or archive per that decision, record the delegate and forwarding position explicitly, then reclaim the licence to the pool and enter any resulting reduction in the queue. Copying a leaver's mail to a personal location, or setting a permanent forward to a manager without a recorded instruction, is not a technical shortcut but a data decision the client must make in writing.

included: the three ordered paths and their standards
capture of the client's written retention and forwarding decision before reclaim
entitlement removal on role change
the return of the seat to the pool and into the reduction queue
the write-back to the service record
excluded: employment, disciplinary or monitoring advice, which is the client's to take from their own adviser
the bulk onboarding performed during the original migration
authoring the client's own device or acceptable-use policy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a departure handled outside the runbook, or a vendor change to mailbox conversion and data-recovery behaviour after licence removal

pros.claim: The leaver path is where the operator's value is most visible to an owner, because it closes an exposure they can immediately understand
pros.example: an owner watching a departing salesperson's access, second factor and phone enrolment removed within the hour of being told, with the mailbox preserved as instructed

pros.claim: A standard joiner path removes an entire class of first-week support tickets and makes new-hire onboarding predictable enough to quote
pros.example: a new employee signing in, finding their groups and shared mailboxes already correct, and never raising a ticket at all

cons.claim: The paths depend entirely on the client telling the operator in time, and small businesses routinely tell nobody until after the person has gone
cons.example: learning of a departure three weeks later during the reconciliation, with the account active throughout

cons.claim: Handling departures places the operator close to disputes it must stay out of, where a helpful action can become evidence in someone else's argument
cons.example: being asked to forward a departing employee's mailbox to their manager during an acrimonious exit

failure_modes: reclaiming the licence before the retention decision, destroying data the client needed
resetting the password but leaving active sessions, application passwords or a registered second factor in place
leaving a permanent forward or delegation in place with no record of who asked for it
letting movers accumulate entitlements until a long-serving employee can reach everything
acting on a departure reported by a colleague rather than by an authorized requester
acceptance_tests: every leaver record shows session revocation, credential reset, second-factor and device removal, the client's written data decision, the mailbox disposition and the licence action, each with a timestamp
no forwarding or delegation exists in any tenant without a recorded instruction naming who asked for it and when
a mover's removed entitlements are listed explicitly, not merely the added ones
revisit_triggers: a departure is discovered during reconciliation rather than reported by the client
a vendor change alters what happens to a mailbox when its licence is removed or converted
the client changes who is responsible for telling the operator about staff changes

nodes.definition: Every cycle, prove that three things agree before any margin is assumed: what the provider invoiced the operator, what the tenant's subscriptions actually are, and what the operator invoiced the client. Work line by line against the change log rather than in totals, because totals hide compensating errors. Explain every variance: a mid-cycle addition and how it was pro-rated, a reduction that took effect on a different date than expected, a promotion that expired, a currency or indirect-tax line, a credit that was agreed and never arrived, a platform or provider fee that is charged separately from the subscription. Confirm that the management fee and any one-off project work were billed once and only once. Then reconcile what was actually collected rather than what was invoiced, because on a pass-through subscription a failed card or an unpaid invoice leaves the operator paying the provider for a service the client's staff are still happily using, and that exposure grows every month it is not addressed. Hold a dunning and suspension position that was stated at the start of the relationship and is applied evenly to everyone, so the awkward conversation is a policy rather than a judgement about a particular client. Margin leakage here is silent, compounds, and is usually discovered only when the operator finally computes what the book actually earned.

included: the three-way line-level comparison against the change log
variance explanation classes
collection status as distinct from invoicing
the stated dunning and suspension policy
chasing agreed credits
excluded: how the spread and the fee were set at the point of sale, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
tax treatment advice, where only the obligation class is named and current rules are verified in the operator's jurisdiction
the provider's own contractual dispute process

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cycle in which realised spread diverges from the expected spread, or a provider billing-platform or fee change

pros.claim: Line-level reconciliation is the only way the operator finds out that the money it believes it earns is the money it actually earns
pros.example: discovering that a promotional rate expired two cycles ago while the client price stayed unchanged, quietly erasing the spread on that account

pros.claim: Tracking collection rather than invoicing surfaces the pass-through exposure early, while it is still one cycle rather than six
pros.example: catching a failed payment method in the first cycle and resolving it before the operator has funded three months of another business's subscriptions

cons.claim: It is unglamorous administrative work with no client-visible output, so it is the first task dropped in a busy month and the last one anyone notices was dropped
cons.example: three cycles passing before anyone examines why the provider invoice grew while the client invoices did not

cons.claim: Applying a suspension policy evenly will eventually mean applying it to a client the operator likes, and not applying it teaches the whole book that the policy is decorative
cons.example: a long-standing client's unpaid invoices being carried for months because the relationship feels too good to risk

failure_modes: reconciling totals instead of lines, so two errors cancel and both persist
assuming margin from a price list rather than verifying it against what the provider actually charged
treating an invoice as revenue before it is collected on a pass-through subscription
letting an agreed credit go unchased because chasing it costs more attention than it returns
improvising a suspension decision per client instead of applying a stated policy
acceptance_tests: every provider invoice line for the cycle is matched to a subscription line and a change-log entry, and every unmatched line has a written explanation
collection status is known for every account, and any account past the stated dunning point has had the stated action taken
the realised spread per account for the cycle is computed from actual charges rather than from a list price
revisit_triggers: a provider price revision, promotion expiry or platform-fee change takes effect
an unexplained variance appears in two consecutive cycles
a payment method fails or an account passes the stated dunning point

nodes.definition: Convert the support promise made at sale into an operating document that the operator can actually staff and the client can actually read. It states the intake channels and which one is authoritative, the covered hours and what happens outside them, a first-response target by severity class expressed as the operator's own commitment and never as a restatement of the vendor's platform commitment, who at the client may raise a request and who may authorize a change, what is included in the recurring fee, what is billable project work, and what is not offered at all. Included work in this business is typically identity and access administration, mail-flow problems inside the suite, licence administration, and custody of the security posture; billable work is typically new applications and integrations, device rebuilds, third-party software that merely shows its symptoms inside the mail client, data recovery beyond the covered path, and anything at a physical site; not offered is the list the operator will refuse consistently, such as personal devices and family accounts. Write the refusal in advance, as a script, because the moment to invent one is never the moment it is needed. The three-tier framing inherited from the sale — handled, escalated, not promised — becomes real here only when it has names, hours, and a queue behind it.

included: intake channels and the authoritative one
hours, severity classes and the operator's own response commitments
the included, billable and not-offered lists
the authorized-requester list
the written refusal script
excluded: the program-imposed support duty and how it was disclosed at sale, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
the vendor's own platform service commitments, which are quoted from their published terms and never adopted as the operator's own
incident containment procedure, which is its own unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured support minutes by class, or a repeated structural miss against a stated response commitment

pros.claim: A written model lets the operator say yes and no quickly and identically to everyone, which is what makes a one-person support function survivable
pros.example: answering a Saturday request about a home printer with the same sentence used for every out-of-scope request, in a minute rather than an hour of guilt

pros.claim: Separating the operator's response commitment from the vendor's platform commitment prevents the most expensive promise in this business
pros.example: not being held to a platform availability figure the operator neither controls nor was ever paid to guarantee

cons.claim: Any published response target becomes a stick, and a solo operator can be genuinely unable to meet one during a single bad week
cons.example: two clients with simultaneous mail-flow problems while the operator is mid-migration for a third

cons.claim: A precise boundary makes the operator look narrower than the informal helper the client thought they were buying, and some buyers value the informality more
cons.example: an owner who liked that the previous provider fixed anything at all, reading the inclusion list as a downgrade

failure_modes: publishing a response target the operator has not staffed and cannot meet in a normal week
restating the vendor's availability commitment as the operator's own promise
leaving the not-offered list unwritten so every refusal is negotiated from scratch
accepting requests through whichever channel each client prefers until nothing is tracked
letting anyone at the client authorize a change because it feels rude to ask
acceptance_tests: the document names intake, hours, severity classes with the operator's own response commitments, and the included, billable and not-offered lists
no client-facing sentence in it repeats a vendor platform commitment as the operator's own
the authorized-requester list for each tenant exists and matches the service record
revisit_triggers: measured minutes show a class of work consuming far more than the fee assumed
a response target is missed repeatedly for structural rather than exceptional reasons
a new service is added to the book that changes what support means

nodes.definition: Get every request into one queue and decide within its first minutes what kind of thing it is, because classification decides ownership, urgency, whether the work is inside the fee, and whether the operator should be touching it at all. The classes that matter in this business are: a vendor platform incident, where the correct action is to check the status source and communicate rather than debug; a tenant configuration problem, which is the operator's to fix; an identity or access problem, which is urgent by default because it usually means someone cannot work or someone can who should not; an endpoint or device problem, which may be in or out of scope depending on the model; a third-party application problem that merely surfaces inside the mail client and is routinely misreported as an email fault; and user education, which is legitimate work and should be recognised as such rather than resented. Intake also captures who asked and whether they are on the authorized list, and starts the elapsed-minutes record that later becomes the cost-to-serve evidence. For a one-person operation the binding constraint is context-switching rather than raw hours, so a stated response rhythm and deliberate batching of non-urgent work protect more capacity than any attempt at instant answers.

included: the single queue and channel discipline
the classification taxonomy and what each class implies
the authorization check at intake
elapsed-minute capture
batching and response rhythm
excluded: the fix procedures for each class
monitoring and alerting products
the decision about what is inside the fee, which the support model already fixed

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cycle whose class distribution shifts sharply, or repeated misclassification at intake leading to wrong ownership

pros.claim: Classifying at intake stops the most expensive mistake in small-shop support, which is debugging someone else's outage for an hour before checking the status source
pros.example: recognising three unrelated clients reporting slow mail within twenty minutes as a platform event rather than three tenant problems

pros.claim: Captured minutes at intake are the only evidence that will exist later when an account has to be re-priced
pros.example: showing a client a year of ticket minutes by class rather than asserting that they take up a lot of time

cons.claim: Insisting on one channel fights the way small-business owners actually work, and enforcing it too hard is read as bureaucracy
cons.example: an owner who will always send a text message at nine in the evening regardless of what the service description says

cons.claim: Classification at intake is done with the least information available and misclassification propagates into ownership and urgency decisions
cons.example: a mail-delivery complaint classified as user education that turns out to be a domain authentication problem affecting every outbound message

failure_modes: letting requests arrive across several channels so no queue is complete
starting work before checking whether the requester is authorized
skipping the platform-status check for a symptom that looks tenant-specific
recording no time at all, which makes every later economic argument unwinnable
treating user education as an interruption rather than as a class of covered work
acceptance_tests: every request in the last cycle exists in the single queue with a class, a requester, an authorization check and elapsed minutes
requests that arrived by other channels were logged into the queue rather than handled invisibly
revisit_triggers: one class dominates the queue for a cycle, which usually means a cause rather than a coincidence
misclassification at intake causes a materially wrong response
a new service or add-on introduces a class the taxonomy does not cover

nodes.definition: Decide, every time, what to do with the request that sits outside what the fee buys: the printer, the accounting package, the personal laptop, the new website, the phrase 'while you're in there'. There are exactly three honest answers and one dishonest one. Do it and log it as a deliberate gift with a value note, which is a fine choice made consciously and occasionally. Quote it as project work with a price and a start date. Decline it and refer it to someone who does that work, which preserves the relationship better than a reluctant attempt. The fourth path, absorbing it silently and repeatedly, is how a good account becomes an unprofitable one and how an operator ends up resenting a client who was never told there was a problem. Keep a drift ledger per account recording absorbed out-of-scope minutes and what they were for, review it at the account review, and use the ledger rather than a feeling when re-pricing or re-scoping, because a client can argue with irritation but not with their own history. The language matters as much as the rule: name what the request is, say what it would cost, offer the alternative, and never make the client feel foolish for asking.

included: the three honest responses and when each applies
the per-account drift ledger
the re-pricing or re-scoping trigger drawn from the ledger
the language of a boundary that keeps the relationship
excluded: the sale-time scope disclosure, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
punitive re-pricing without ledger evidence
the definition of what is in scope, which the support model fixed

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a drift ledger that changes an account's contribution, or the same out-of-scope class recurring across the book

pros.claim: A ledger turns an emotional conversation into an evidential one and gives the operator a defensible basis for changing a price
pros.example: showing an owner a year of small absorbed favours totalling a meaningful share of a month, and proposing a scope change rather than a complaint

pros.claim: A deliberate, logged gift is a genuine relationship asset, whereas the same work absorbed silently earns nothing because nobody knows it happened
pros.example: an invoice line showing an out-of-scope fix at no charge, which the client reads as generosity rather than as included

cons.claim: Enforcing a boundary at the wrong moment can cost an account that was otherwise healthy, and the moment is rarely convenient
cons.example: declining a small favour during a week when the client is already unhappy about an unrelated outage

cons.claim: Maintaining the ledger costs attention during exactly the interruptions it is meant to measure, so it is systematically under-recorded
cons.example: twenty minutes of phone help on a third-party application that never reaches the ledger because it happened in a corridor conversation

failure_modes: absorbing out-of-scope work silently until the account is unprofitable
declining without offering any alternative, which reads as unhelpfulness rather than as a boundary
re-pricing from irritation rather than from the ledger
gifting work without logging it, so it accrues no goodwill and distorts the cost measurement
letting one client's exception become the whole book's expectation
acceptance_tests: every out-of-scope request in the last cycle resolved into one of the three responses and appears in the ledger with minutes and a note
any re-pricing proposal cites ledger entries rather than general impressions
revisit_triggers: one account's drift ledger passes the point where it materially changes that account's economics
the same out-of-scope class appears across several accounts, suggesting the service description is wrong rather than the clients
an account review results in a scope change

nodes.definition: Know precisely when a problem stops being the operator's to solve, how to hand it upward, and what to say to the client while someone else fixes it. The trigger is evidential rather than emotional: the fault has been reproduced, the tenant-side causes the operator can test have been ruled out, and the remaining explanation lives in the platform or in a provider-controlled layer. Assemble the evidence pack the provider or vendor will ask for before opening anything, because a case opened without it simply returns a request for it: tenant identifier, affected users, timestamps with time zone, message identifiers or traces, the exact error text, reproduction steps, and what has already been ruled out. Choose the route the transacting model actually requires, which may be a case with the indirect provider, a case with the vendor, or watching a published status source when the answer is that nothing can be done. Then run the parallel obligation that clients actually judge: a plain-language statement of what is known, what is not, what is being done and when the next update comes, delivered at the stated interval even when there is nothing new, because silence during someone else's outage is what clients remember. Never restate the vendor's service commitment as the operator's own promise, and never invent a restoration time the operator does not control.

included: the evidential escalation trigger
the evidence pack contents
route selection under the transacting model
the client communication cadence during an upstream incident
the prohibition on inventing restoration times
excluded: negotiating remedies, credits or program-level commitments with the provider, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
building status monitoring or notification products
containment of a security compromise, which is its own unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the provider's case process or evidence requirements, or an incident whose communication gap was visible to clients

pros.claim: A prepared evidence pack materially shortens the round trip with a provider, which is the only part of an upstream incident the operator can influence
pros.example: opening a mail-flow case with traces, identifiers and ruled-out causes attached rather than a sentence saying that mail is slow

pros.claim: A fixed update cadence during an outage protects the relationship better than a fast fix, because clients judge the communication they can see
pros.example: hourly updates to every affected client during a platform event, each one honest that there is nothing new

cons.claim: Escalation surrenders control of the timeline while leaving the operator fully responsible for the relationship, which is an uncomfortable and unavoidable asymmetry
cons.example: waiting on a case while a client asks every hour when their mail will work

cons.claim: Escalating too early trains the provider to treat the operator's cases as unfiltered and wastes the operator's credibility on the day it matters
cons.example: opening a case for a symptom that a routine tenant-side check would have explained in five minutes

failure_modes: opening a case without the evidence pack and losing a cycle to the request for it
debugging a platform incident for hours because the status source was never checked
going silent with clients while waiting on the provider
inventing a restoration estimate to fill an uncomfortable silence
quoting the vendor's availability commitment to a client as though the operator had made it
acceptance_tests: every escalation in the last cycle records the ruled-out tenant-side causes and the evidence pack that accompanied it
affected clients received updates at the stated interval for the duration of the incident, including updates with no new information
revisit_triggers: the provider or vendor changes its case-handling process, routes or required evidence
an incident exposes a communication gap the cadence did not cover
cases are repeatedly returned for missing information

nodes.definition: Measure what each account actually consumes so that price, scope and exit decisions rest on this book's own history rather than on how the operator feels about a client. Capture four kinds of time cheaply: support minutes by class from the queue, out-of-scope minutes from the drift ledger, administrative minutes from the reconciliation, true-up and billing cycles, and incident time when it occurs. Set that against the account's realised contribution, meaning the verified subscription spread from the billing reconciliation plus the management fee, net of payment processing, provider platform charges and any bad debt, to produce a contribution per account-month and a cost-to-serve floor below which an account should not be accepted or retained. The measurement has to be crude enough to survive contact with a busy week — a rough timer and an honest rounding rule beat a precise system nobody keeps — and it must be maintained continuously, because a cost argument reconstructed from memory at the moment of a re-pricing conversation is exactly the argument a client can refuse. Its purpose is not to punish demanding clients; it is to give the operator three evidenced options where previously there was only endurance: re-price, re-scope, or end the relationship cleanly. Note also that time spent is not the same as value delivered, and the quietest accounts are frequently the most profitable and the least appreciated.

included: the four time-capture categories
realised contribution per account-month from verified charges
the cost-to-serve floor and how it is set from the operator's own records
the re-price, re-scope or exit decision options
excluded: the sale-time seat-economics model that predicted the number, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
accounting or tax treatment advice
any industry benchmark or published margin figure used in place of measurement

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a full cycle of captured minutes, or a change in provider platform and payment charges that moves realised contribution

pros.claim: Measured minutes convert an uncomfortable intuition into a decision the operator can defend to the client and to itself
pros.example: an account that always felt heavy turning out to consume several times the administrative time of a similar-sized one, entirely through third-party application questions

pros.claim: A floor expressed per account-month lets the operator say no to a new prospect on evidence rather than on instinct
pros.example: declining a two-seat account whose expected administrative time alone would sit below the measured floor

cons.claim: Time capture is self-reported by the busiest person in the business and systematically undercounts exactly the interruptions that matter most
cons.example: a stream of two-minute phone questions that never appears anywhere in the record

cons.claim: Optimising a small book purely on measured contribution can drive out clients who bring referrals, reputation or learning that the measurement cannot see
cons.example: exiting a low-contribution account that had introduced three others in the same trade

failure_modes: computing contribution from list prices rather than from what the provider actually charged
measuring only ticket time and ignoring the administrative and billing cycles, which are the steady cost
starting the measurement at the moment of the re-pricing conversation, when it is worthless as evidence
treating the floor as a secret rather than as a rule the operator applies consistently
confusing a quiet account with a low-value one
acceptance_tests: every account has captured minutes for at least one complete cycle across support, out-of-scope and administrative categories
contribution per account-month is computed from verified charges and fees, not from list prices
each account below the floor has a written decision attached: re-price, re-scope, or exit, with a date
revisit_triggers: an account crosses the floor in either direction
the provider changes platform or payment charges that feed the contribution calculation
a scope change or re-price takes effect and the effect on minutes needs verification

nodes.definition: Run a scheduled, repeatable inspection of each tenant against the baseline it was delivered with, because this is the recurring work that makes a subscription feel like a service rather than a line on a card statement. The checklist is stable and boring on purpose: multi-factor coverage and every exclusion with its reason, the count and use of privileged roles including any account created since the last review, the state and custody of break-glass credentials, legacy or basic authentication protocols still enabled, mailbox forwarding and delegation rules with particular attention to external destinations, external sharing and guest access, third-party application consents that users granted without anyone noticing, retention and backup configuration as actually deployed against what the client believes, security features the client already pays for in their current licence tier but has never had enabled, and accounts that have never signed in or have been dormant for a long period. The output is a dated findings list where every entry has a severity, a recommended fix, an owner and a date, and where anything the client declines is recorded as a decision they made, with who declined it and when. The value is not the list; it is the judgement about which two or three findings actually matter in this particular business, stated in the owner's language rather than in vendor terminology.

included: the repeatable checklist against the delivered baseline
the dated findings list with severity, fix, owner and date
the declined-risk record
the licence-tier feature check for capabilities already paid for
prioritisation into what matters for this business
excluded: designing and building the baseline itself, which belongs to the tenant-setup KB
penetration testing, red teaming and forensic investigation
compliance certification or an assertion that the client is compliant with anything

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an incident, a vendor default or control change, or a licence-tier change at a client that alters what can be checked

pros.claim: A recurring review is the clearest recurring justification for a recurring fee, and it produces the evidence the account review is later built from
pros.example: a review that finds an external forwarding rule on a director's mailbox nobody had noticed, and closes it the same day

pros.claim: The licence-tier feature check regularly improves a client's security without selling them anything, which is the strongest possible proof the operator is not simply upselling
pros.example: enabling a protection the client has been paying for since the original purchase and never had switched on

cons.claim: A checklist run without judgement produces a long undifferentiated list that owners ignore, and the second such list is ignored faster than the first
cons.example: a review handing an owner twenty findings of mixed severity with no statement of which two matter this quarter

cons.claim: Findings the client declines accumulate into a risk the operator is now documented as knowing about, which is uncomfortable and cannot be undone by forgetting it
cons.example: an owner who repeatedly refuses to enforce a second factor on their own account while the operator holds administrative access to the tenant

failure_modes: delivering a scan output instead of a judgement about this business
checking configuration but never checking what the client's current tier already entitles them to
leaving declined findings undocumented so the same conversation repeats every review
reviewing only what is easy to see and never the forwarding, delegation and consent surfaces where quiet compromise lives
using findings as a sales instrument rather than as a maintenance record
acceptance_tests: every checklist item is answered for every tenant in the review cycle, with unknowns recorded as unknown
every finding carries a severity, a recommended fix, an owner and a date, and every decline names who declined and when
the review names the small number of findings that matter most for this business in the owner's own terms
revisit_triggers: an incident or near-miss anywhere in the book adds a check
the vendor changes a default, deprecates a protocol or introduces a control that belongs on the list
a client's licence tier changes, altering which capabilities exist
a review finds the same declined item for the third time

nodes.definition: Between scheduled reviews, watch the small number of changes that actually precede trouble, at a volume one person can sustain indefinitely. The signals worth having are the ones that are rare and meaningful: a new assignment of a privileged role, a new or modified mailbox rule that forwards or redirects mail outside the organisation, a mailbox rule that moves or deletes messages in a way that hides them, a newly registered authentication method or an exclusion added for a privileged user, a sign-in pattern the tenant has never seen before, and a new third-party application consent. Each signal needs three things before it is turned on: a named owner, a triage step written in advance, and an expected volume, because a watchlist that produces noise is muted within a month and a muted watchlist is more dangerous than no watchlist at all, since everyone still believes it is working. Be honest that the availability and depth of these signals depend on the licence tier the client actually holds and on what the vendor exposes today; say plainly what is and is not visible in this tenant rather than implying a coverage the tier does not provide. This is a small operator's watch, not a monitoring service: it is bounded, it is not continuous, and the client should be told so in the same words every time.

included: the signal shortlist and why each is on it
owner, triage step and expected volume per signal
tuning to keep the volume sustainable
the honest statement of what the client's tier makes visible
excluded: around-the-clock monitoring or a security-operations service
building detection or alerting products
the scheduled review itself
any implication of continuous coverage the operator does not provide

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured alert volume per signal, a tier change at a client, or an incident that no enabled signal surfaced

pros.claim: A handful of well-chosen signals catches the specific changes that precede business-email compromise, which is the failure mode this client base actually suffers
pros.example: an alert on a newly created rule forwarding a bookkeeper's mail to an external address, caught before an invoice was altered

pros.claim: Declaring the limits of the watch protects both parties and is repeatable, unlike a vague sense that the operator is keeping an eye on things
pros.example: telling a client in writing that sign-in anomaly detection is not available at their current tier, and what that means

cons.claim: Every added signal is unpaid triage time, and the operator bears the cost of noise while the client bears the benefit of coverage
cons.example: a fortnight of chasing legitimate travel sign-ins that each took twenty minutes to close

cons.claim: A watch that exists creates an expectation of vigilance the operator cannot honour outside working hours, which is precisely when these events happen
cons.example: a compromise beginning on a Friday evening and detected on Monday morning by a watch nobody promised was continuous

failure_modes: enabling everything available and muting all of it within a month
letting a client believe the watch is continuous monitoring
having a signal with no written triage step, so its first firing produces improvisation
not re-checking that the signals still work after a vendor or tier change
watching only for identity events and ignoring rule and consent changes
acceptance_tests: each enabled signal has an owner, a written triage step and an expected volume, and the actual volume has been checked against it
the client has a written statement of what is watched, what is not, and what their tier does not make visible
revisit_triggers: a signal's volume rises to the point where it is being ignored
a client's licence tier changes
an incident occurs that no enabled signal would have surfaced
the vendor changes what the tenant exposes or how

nodes.definition: Recognise the obligation classes that keep recurring once the operator is administering someone else's business data, and handle each one without drifting into practising law. The classes a small reseller meets repeatedly are: acting as a processor-type party over client data, where the operator acts on the client's documented instructions and not on its own initiative; retention and legal-hold requests, where the safe default is to preserve rather than delete and to say so; export and search requests, including for a departed employee's mail, which almost always arrive urgently and informally; access requests made by individuals, which belong to the client as the controlling party and are routed to them rather than answered by the operator; breach-notification duties, where a clock may start on the client and the operator's job is to inform them promptly and factually rather than to interpret the deadline; employee-monitoring requests, which are legally sensitive in most places and require written instruction from an authorized signer; sector-specific rules a client asserts about their own trade; and questions about where data physically sits. In every class the procedure is the same shape: recognise the class, require written instruction from someone with authority, preserve rather than destroy while it is unclear, produce records of what was done, and tell the client to verify current rules in their own jurisdiction with their own adviser. Never promise a compliance outcome and never characterise a legal position.

included: recognition of the recurring obligation classes
the written-instruction requirement before acting
preservation as the default under uncertainty
records of actions taken
the referral language sending the client to their own adviser and current local rules
excluded: legal, tax, insurance or compliance advice in any form
certifying or asserting that a client is compliant
the sale-time mapping of obligations, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
making the notification decision on the client's behalf

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a request that does not fit a named class, a change in vendor hold or export behaviour, or a client asserting a new regulatory position

pros.claim: Naming the class converts a frightening request into a known procedure and stops the operator improvising under pressure
pros.example: receiving an urgent demand to delete a departed employee's mailbox during a dispute, and recognising it as a preservation question rather than a deletion task

pros.claim: Written instruction protects the client as much as the operator, because it forces the decision to be made by the party who is entitled to make it
pros.example: a monitoring request that the owner reconsiders once it has to be written down and signed

cons.claim: Insisting on written instruction slows down clients in exactly the moments they feel most urgent, and some will experience it as obstruction
cons.example: an owner who wants a mailbox opened immediately being asked for a scoped written authorization first

cons.claim: The boundary between recognising a class and giving advice is genuinely narrow, and a helpful sentence can cross it without either party noticing
cons.example: explaining what a notification deadline probably is, which is precisely the interpretation the operator must not supply

failure_modes: deleting data during a dispute because a client asked urgently
answering an individual's access request directly instead of routing it to the client
interpreting a notification deadline or a legal duty for a client
acting on a verbal instruction for a sensitive action because the requester was the owner's spouse or manager
promising that a configuration makes the client compliant with something
acceptance_tests: every action taken under one of these classes is traceable to a written instruction from a named authorized signer, with date and scope
no client-facing communication states a deadline, a legal conclusion or a compliance outcome, and each refers the client to their own adviser and to current rules in their jurisdiction
requests that would destroy data during an unresolved matter were preserved and escalated rather than executed
revisit_triggers: a client asserts a new sector rule or a new data-location requirement
an obligation class appears that the list does not name
the vendor changes retention, hold or export behaviour
the operator's own jurisdiction or a client's jurisdiction changes materially

nodes.definition: Have a written procedure for the first hour of a suspected compromise in a managed tenant, because this is the event that either proves the whole service or ends the relationship. The pattern in this client base is business-email compromise: a credential phished, a session token stolen, rules created to hide replies, and an attempt to redirect a payment. Contain first, in a known order: revoke active sessions and refresh tokens, reset the credential and re-register the second factor, find and remove attacker-created forwarding, redirect and hide-message rules, revoke recently granted third-party application consents, and check for privileged-role changes and newly created accounts. Preserve before cleaning: export the rule contents, the message traces, the sign-in and audit records and the current mailbox permissions to a dated evidence store, because these age out of retention and a client's insurer or adviser will ask for exactly the thing that was deleted while tidying. Tell the client immediately in plain language, stating what is known, what is not, and what is being done, and warn explicitly about the payment path if any invoice, bank detail or payment instruction may have been touched, because that is where the money is actually lost. Name the operator's limits in the same conversation: this is containment and restoration of service, not forensic attribution, and the client's insurer, bank, accountant, lawyer and, where applicable, the authorities have roles the operator must not improvise or delay. Log every action with time and authorization.
