included: the ordered containment class of actions
evidence preservation before cleanup
immediate plain-language client notification including the payment-fraud path
the statement of the operator's limits and the parties with their own roles
the timed action log
excluded: forensic investigation, attribution and expert testimony
legal, insurance or regulatory advice, including whether and when the client must notify anyone
negotiating with an attacker
recovering funds, which is the client's bank's and adviser's territory

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: any incident or near-miss in the book, or a vendor change to revocation, consent or audit-log retention behaviour

pros.claim: A written first-hour order removes decision-making from the worst possible moment and is the difference between containment and a week of uncertainty
pros.example: revoking sessions and removing hidden inbox rules within minutes of a bookkeeper reporting a strange sign-in prompt

pros.claim: Preserving evidence before cleaning is the step that clients and their advisers value most in hindsight and that operators most often skip
pros.example: having dated exports of the rules and sign-in records when the client's insurer asks two months later

cons.claim: Containment consumes hours that no recurring fee anticipated, at an hour of the day nobody agreed to, and the account may never repay them
cons.example: an entire weekend spent on a five-seat client whose monthly fee is a small fraction of the time spent

cons.claim: Acting decisively inside someone else's business during a crisis creates real exposure to blame for consequences the operator did not cause
cons.example: a forced credential reset locking out an owner during a bidding deadline, which becomes the thing they remember

failure_modes: cleaning up before preserving evidence, destroying the record the client's adviser will need
resetting the password but leaving sessions, tokens and application consents alive
waiting for certainty before telling the client
failing to warn about the payment-diversion path while focusing on the mailbox
drifting into forensic or legal statements the operator is not qualified to make
acting without recording what was done, when, and on whose authorization
acceptance_tests: the written procedure exists with the containment order, the preservation list and the notification triggers, and can be executed by someone reading it for the first time
for any incident, a dated evidence export exists that predates the cleanup actions
the client notification record shows plain-language content, the payment-path warning where relevant, and the statement of what the operator does not do
every action taken appears in a timed log with the authorization it relied on
revisit_triggers: any incident or near-miss, which must feed a procedure change and a posture check across the book
a vendor change to session revocation, consent or audit-retention behaviour
a client's insurer or adviser asks for something the preservation list did not capture

nodes.definition: Govern every expansion conversation with one rule: nothing is proposed unless a dated, tenant-specific observation supports it. Qualifying evidence is a posture-review finding in this tenant, a ticket pattern in this account, a restore or recovery that was attempted and was not possible, a measured gap between what the client believes they have and what they actually have, a change in how the client works, or a request the client made themselves. Disqualifying material is everything the industry usually leans on: breach statistics from elsewhere, anecdotes about other businesses, implied liability, manufactured deadlines, a vendor promotion's end date presented as the client's urgency, and any campaign driven by an attach rate or a partner target rather than by a tenant. The proposal itself must state the observation and its date, what the add-on would change and explicitly what it would not, what it costs to buy and what it costs the operator to run, the do-nothing option with its honest consequence, and the operator's own interest where a spread is involved. Bundling an add-on into a renewal so that it passes unnoticed is prohibited: it must be accepted separately and knowingly. The working test is simple and severe — could the operator show the client the exact evidence line that produced the recommendation, and would the client recognise it as a true description of their own business?

included: the qualifying and disqualifying evidence classes
the required structure of a proposal
the do-nothing option and disclosure of the operator's interest
the prohibition on bundling an add-on into a renewal
the showable-evidence test
excluded: the sale-time right-sizing of the original licence mix, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
the technical content of each service, which the expansion catalogue holds
any argument for a product the operator cannot itself run

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a proposal that could not be traced to a dated tenant observation, or an incentive campaign that changes the pressure on this rule

pros.claim: An evidence rule makes the operator's recommendations believable precisely because they are rare, which is the entire basis of the trusted-operator position
pros.example: a client accepting a backup proposal without hesitation because the last three reviews recommended nothing at all

pros.claim: Stating the do-nothing option and the operator's own interest removes the pressure that makes small-business owners defensive, and it usually shortens the decision
pros.example: an owner deciding within a day because the recommendation named what would not change and what it earned the operator

cons.claim: The rule blocks revenue the operator can plainly see is available, in a business where expansion is the main growth lever available to a small book
cons.example: declining to raise device management with a client whose tenant shows no evidence of the problem it solves, in a month when income was short

cons.claim: Waiting for tenant-specific evidence means some risks are only addressed after the client has been harmed by them
cons.example: a backup conversation that becomes easy only after an unrecoverable deletion that a proposal months earlier might have prevented

failure_modes: retro-fitting a justification onto a recommendation the operator had already decided to make
using borrowed breach statistics or a competitor's incident as the evidence
presenting a vendor promotion deadline as the client's own urgency
bundling an add-on into a renewal statement so it is accepted without a separate decision
omitting the do-nothing option because it weakens the proposal
running an attach-rate campaign across the book instead of examining tenants one at a time
acceptance_tests: every live proposal names a dated tenant-specific observation, the do-nothing option and its consequence, and what the add-on does not cover
no proposal in the file cites an external statistic, anecdote or vendor deadline as its justification
no add-on appears inside a renewal statement without a separate, recorded acceptance
where the operator earns a spread on the add-on, the proposal says so
revisit_triggers: a proposal is declined, which requires recording the reason rather than re-pitching
a vendor or provider launches an incentive campaign, which is the moment this rule is most under pressure
an incident in the book creates real evidence that changes what should be proposed to whom

nodes.definition: Know the adjacent services well enough to describe them honestly, and know whether this operator can actually run them before any of them is offered. For third-party backup of the suite, the honest account starts with what the platform already does — deleted-item recovery, retention policies, recoverable-item windows, all with vendor-defined durations that must be read from current documentation — and then states precisely what a separate backup adds: restore granularity, retention beyond the native window, retention of a departed user's data after their licence is gone, and protection against deletions made from inside the tenant by someone with legitimate access. For security add-ons, the first step is nearly always a licence-overlap check, because a large share of what is sold as an upgrade is a capability the client is already paying for and has never had enabled. For device management, the honest framing is that the software is the small part and the ongoing support burden of enrolled devices is the large part. For archiving and other resold subscriptions, the question is whether the operator is adding management or merely adding an invoice. For every entry the catalogue records four things: the specific failure it addresses, what it explicitly does not cover, the recurring labour it adds to the operator, and a capability test the operator must have passed — a restore actually performed and timed, a policy actually authored and supportable — before the service may be proposed at all. If the operator cannot operate it, the honest moves are to refer it or to decline it, not to learn on a client's data.

included: per-service statement of the failure addressed and what is not covered
the native-behaviour and licence-overlap check performed first
the recurring labour each service adds to the operator
the capability test that must be passed before offering
the refer-or-decline path
excluded: enterprise product selection and vendor-neutral security consulting
any performance, prevention or recovery guarantee beyond the vendor's published terms
the evidence rule that decides whether a proposal may be made at all, which is its own unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a vendor change to native retention or included features, or a capability test that fails or reveals unexpected operating labour

pros.claim: Naming the native behaviour before selling the add-on is the single most credibility-building sentence available to this business
pros.example: telling a client what their suite already recovers and for how long, and only then explaining the gap a separate backup covers

pros.claim: A capability test stops the operator selling a promise it cannot keep, which is the failure that ends relationships permanently
pros.example: performing and timing a full mailbox restore in a test tenant before quoting backup to a client

cons.claim: Every added service multiplies the operator's own support surface and the number of vendors whose changes it must track, which a small shop absorbs badly
cons.example: a device-management add-on turning every new laptop in every client into an enrolment ticket the operator now owns

cons.claim: Honest description of native capability regularly kills a sale the operator could easily have made, and the discipline is invisible to everyone except the operator
cons.example: a client deciding they do not need backup after hearing what their retention policy already covers

failure_modes: selling a capability the client's current tier already includes
quoting a service whose restore or policy the operator has never actually exercised
describing what an add-on protects against without describing what it does not
adding an adjacent subscription that the operator merely bills and does not manage
underestimating the recurring labour a service adds and pricing only the licence
acceptance_tests: every catalogue entry states the failure addressed, the explicit non-coverage, the recurring labour added, and the capability test that has been passed with its date
no service is offered whose capability test is untested or failed, and the refer-or-decline alternative is recorded where that applies
a licence-overlap check against the client's current tier is recorded before any security add-on is proposed
revisit_triggers: a vendor changes native retention, recovery or included-feature behaviour
a client's licence tier changes and absorbs a capability the catalogue sells
an add-on proves unsupportable in practice after being sold
a restore or policy test fails or takes materially longer than assumed

nodes.definition: Run the anniversary instead of being run by it. Build the calendar backwards from each subscription's renewal date through its notice and adjustment windows so that every date at which the client could still act is marked before it arrives. Before the term relocks, run the pre-renewal work: reconcile seats so the quantity that renews is the quantity actually needed, close or record open posture findings, and clear the pending-reduction queue. Then send a written renewal statement that says what renews, at what quantity, on what term, at what price, on what date, and what the client may still change and by when — before the automatic renewal happens, not in the invoice afterwards. Supplier price revisions and promotional expiries are passed through with the change named, its effective date given, its origin stated plainly as a supplier change, and the operator's own management fee shown as a separate line so a pass-through can never be mistaken for a quiet margin increase; if the operator chooses to absorb a rise, say that too, because unexplained stability is as confusing as unexplained increases. This is also the moment where an unrelated add-on must not be smuggled in. A renewal that arrives as a surprise invoice is the most common self-inflicted churn event in this business, and it is entirely preventable with a calendar and one honest letter.

included: the backwards-built renewal calendar with notice and adjustment windows
the pre-renewal reconciliation and findings close-out
the written renewal statement and its required contents
supplier price-change pass-through with separated fee lines
the recorded decision where the operator absorbs a change
excluded: the original term choice and pricing at the point of sale, which belongs to the reseller-programs KB
negotiating program pricing with a provider
introducing a new service at renewal, which requires its own evidence and separate acceptance

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an announced supplier price or term change, or a renewal where the client was surprised by something the statement should have contained

pros.claim: A statement sent before the renewal converts the most dangerous moment in the relationship into evidence that the operator works for the client
pros.example: telling a client six weeks ahead that they could drop three seats before the window closes, and executing it

pros.claim: Separating supplier changes from the operator's own fee makes an unavoidable price rise survivable, because the client can see what it is
pros.example: a statement showing an increased subscription line, an unchanged management fee, and the date the supplier's change takes effect

cons.claim: Disclosing everything before the renewal invites the reduction conversation the operator would rather not have, and some clients will use it
cons.example: a client reducing four seats they would never have noticed if the invoice had simply repeated

cons.claim: The calendar work is front-loaded and the anniversary dates are set by decisions made long before, so the operator inherits a workload it did not design
cons.example: three tenants with subscriptions bought at different times producing renewal work in most months of the year

failure_modes: letting an automatic renewal happen and explaining it afterwards
relocking a term on a quantity that the reconciliation would have reduced
presenting a supplier increase as if it were the operator's own decision, or vice versa
burying a new add-on inside a renewal statement
missing a notice window and telling the client the reduction is impossible without saying why
acceptance_tests: every renewal in the period has a dated written statement sent before the notice window closed, naming quantity, term, price, date and what may still be changed
the pre-renewal reconciliation and the posture findings position are recorded before the term relocks
supplier changes and the operator's own fee appear as separate lines, and any absorbed change is stated
revisit_triggers: a supplier price revision, promotional expiry or term restructure is announced
a notice or adjustment window is missed for any account
a renewal produces a reduction request the operator could not execute
anniversary alignment changes in a tenant

nodes.definition: Read the quiet signals that precede a client leaving, because in this business the loud ones arrive only with the notice. The signals worth watching are: a seat count shrinking for reasons that were never discussed; tickets stopping altogether, which usually means someone else is being asked; tickets spiking with an unfamiliar irritation in them; invoice queries appearing after a year of silence; the arrival of a new office manager, bookkeeper or technically-confident employee; a change of owner, accountant or bank; a sudden interest in what exactly the fee covers; a request for the tenant's own global administrator credentials; a slow or absent response to a renewal statement that previously came back the same day; an acquisition or a merger; and a stated plan to bring things in-house. Each signal has a response that is a conversation rather than a discount: ask directly, early, and while the decision is still open, because a client who has already chosen a successor is being polite rather than negotiating. Time the conversation relative to the renewal calendar so it happens before the window rather than during it. And accept, without pressure tactics, that some accounts should leave: an account sitting below the cost-to-serve floor whose owner no longer values the work is not a retention problem, and the honest response is a clean exit rather than a discount that locks in a bad relationship.

included: the leading-signal list and what each usually means
the conversation-shaped response and its timing against the renewal calendar
the honest decision to let an account go
the link from signals to the account review
excluded: discount-driven or lock-in retention tactics
the sale-time disqualification rules, which belong to the reseller-programs KB
any attempt to make leaving technically difficult

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an account that left with no recorded signal, or a signal that repeatedly fires on healthy accounts

pros.claim: Most of these signals appear months before a notice, which is the only period in which anything can actually be changed
pros.example: noticing that a client who used to raise several tickets a month has raised none for a quarter, and asking why before the renewal

pros.claim: Deciding in advance which accounts the operator would let go removes desperation from the conversation and usually improves the outcome
pros.example: responding to a below-floor account's in-housing plan by offering a clean handover rather than an unsustainable discount

cons.claim: The signals are ambiguous and over-reading them produces anxious behaviour that clients notice and dislike
cons.example: reading a quiet quarter as disengagement when the client was simply busy and content

cons.claim: Acting on a signal forces a conversation that can itself crystallise a decision the client had not yet made
cons.example: asking whether a new technical hire changes the arrangement, and putting the idea into the owner's head

failure_modes: learning about the decision from the notice
responding to every signal with a price reduction
waiting until the renewal window to ask a question that needed asking a quarter earlier
fighting to retain an account that is below the floor and unhappy
treating a request for the client's own administrator credentials as a threat rather than as their right
acceptance_tests: each account has a current signal position reviewed on the same cadence as the account review
every signal acted on has a recorded conversation and outcome, and no response consisted solely of a discount
revisit_triggers: an account leaves without any signal having been recorded, which means the list is wrong
a signal fires on an account that is above the floor and healthy
a client's ownership, management or banking arrangements change

nodes.definition: Hold a periodic review with each client and put one page in front of them, because managed email is invisible when it works and an invisible service is the easiest line on a bank statement to cancel. The page reports what was handled, in ticket counts by class with a sentence about what they actually were; what changed in posture, listing findings closed and, just as importantly, findings the client declined with the risk they chose to accept; what was administered, including joiners, leavers, seats reclaimed and the money that reclaim saved them; what is queued, including pending reductions with their dates; and what is recommended, each item carrying the dated observation that produced it. It also states plainly what the operator did not do and does not cover, because a review that only lists wins slowly re-teaches the client that everything is included. Every number on the page comes from the operator's own records: no invented avoided-loss figure, no borrowed breach statistic, no return-on-investment claim that cannot be traced to a line in this client's own history. The review is also where the drift ledger becomes a re-pricing conversation held on evidence, and where the client's plans for the coming year surface early enough to be work rather than emergencies.

included: the one-page artifact and its sections
sourcing every figure from the operator's own records
the declined-risk restatement
the drift-ledger re-pricing conversation
the forward look at the client's own plans
excluded: marketing collateral and case studies
any avoided-loss, benchmark or return-on-investment claim that cannot be traced to this client's history
the sale-time positioning and wedge argument, which belong to the reseller-programs KB

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client disputing a figure on the review page, or a review cycle that is skipped across several accounts

pros.claim: A page of the client's own history is the most durable defence against the cheaper quote, because the alternative provider has no equivalent
pros.example: an owner seeing a year of leavers processed, seats reclaimed and findings closed on one page during the month a competitor's flyer arrives

pros.claim: Restating declined risks each time moves an uncomfortable decision from the operator's conscience back to where it belongs
pros.example: a third listing of an unenforced second factor on the owner's account finally producing agreement

cons.claim: The review costs unbilled preparation time per account and lands hardest on the smallest clients, who are least able to fund it
cons.example: half a day of preparation across a set of tiny accounts whose combined monthly fees barely cover it

cons.claim: An honest page also documents what the operator failed to do, which will occasionally be the thing the client remembers from the meeting
cons.example: a queued reduction that was missed appearing in the same table as the work that went well

failure_modes: inventing an avoided-loss or return figure to make the page look stronger
listing only successes so the client re-learns that everything is included
skipping the review for small accounts, which are precisely the ones that churn quietly
presenting recommendations without their dated evidence lines
using the review as a sales meeting rather than as a record
acceptance_tests: every figure on the page traces to a record the operator holds, and no external statistic or avoided-loss estimate appears
declined findings are restated with the date they were declined and by whom
the page states at least one thing the operator does not cover or did not do
revisit_triggers: an account misses its review cycle
a client questions a figure on the page
the drift ledger or the cost measurement changes an account's economics enough to require a scope conversation

nodes.definition: Write the exit procedure before it is needed and show it to the client at the start of the relationship, because how an operator behaves on the way out is the clearest evidence of how it held the access all along. On instruction from the authorized signer, confirmed in writing, the sequence is: hand over tenant ownership properly, meaning a global administrator account that genuinely belongs to the client with credentials transferred by a secure route and recovery contacts changed to them; transfer or release the subscriptions to the client or their incoming partner using whatever relationship-transfer mechanism the program currently provides, with its timing and any term consequences named in advance rather than discovered; return the service record, the environment documentation and the change log; remove the operator's delegated access, any accounts it holds inside the tenant and every stored credential, and confirm the removal to the client in writing; settle final billing honestly, including any committed term that genuinely continues and any credit that is genuinely owed; and delete or return client data held outside the tenant according to the agreement. Nothing is withheld as leverage at any point: not a domain, not a tenant, not a credential, not a backup, not documentation, whatever the state of the final invoice, which is a separate matter to be resolved as a debt rather than as a hostage. A clean exit is a referral source, and it is the final proof that the access was always held on the client's behalf.

included: written confirmation of the instruction from the authorized signer
tenant ownership handover and recovery-contact transfer
subscription transfer or release under the current program mechanism with timing named
return of documentation and records
access and credential removal confirmed in writing
final billing and data return or deletion
excluded: debt collection and contract-dispute strategy, which is a separate matter with its own advisers
punitive exit terms or any technical friction designed to make leaving harder
retaining any access for possible future convenience

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a program change to transfer mechanics, or an exit that exposed a step the procedure did not cover

pros.claim: A documented, unpunitive exit converts departures into referrals and removes the fear that makes clients cling to a bad relationship in the first place
pros.example: an incoming provider telling a shared contact that the handover was the cleanest they had received

pros.claim: Removing access with written confirmation closes the operator's own largest residual liability, which otherwise persists silently for years
pros.example: a confirmation record showing that administrative access to a former client's tenant was removed on a named date

cons.claim: Exits arrive at the worst moments and consume unpaid hours from an account that is already leaving, with no commercial return
cons.example: a full day of handover work for a client whose final invoice is small and whose replacement is a relative

cons.claim: Transfer mechanics are program-controlled and their timing can create genuine consequences for the client that the operator can explain but not prevent
cons.example: a subscription transfer that must wait for a specific point in the billing arrangement, which the incoming partner blames on the outgoing one

failure_modes: withholding credentials, documentation or a domain until an invoice is paid
leaving delegated access or an operator-owned account behind after the engagement ends
acting on a departure instruction from someone who is not the authorized signer
handing over a tenant without transferring recovery contacts, so the client cannot recover their own environment
failing to name transfer timing consequences until they have already bitten
acceptance_tests: the exit procedure exists in writing, was shown to the client at the start, and can be executed from the document alone
for every completed exit, a written confirmation exists that all delegated access, operator accounts and stored credentials were removed, with dates
tenant ownership, recovery contacts, documentation and records were transferred, and nothing was withheld pending payment
revisit_triggers: the program changes its subscription transfer or relationship-termination mechanism
an exit reveals a step the procedure did not cover
an access review finds residual access to a former client

edges.why_related: the fields the per-tenant record must carry are dictated by the activities the operating rhythm commits the operator to performing
access can only be scoped, re-attested and revoked against a record that says which tenants exist, who the authorized signer is and what the authorization covers
the term register is the subscription section of the service record and cannot be built before the subscription inventory exists
the reconciliation compares live tenant state against the recorded baseline, quantities and authorized-requester list
there is nothing to execute or queue until the variance list has classified every difference with an action
whether a reduction can happen today or must be queued to a date is answered entirely by the dated term and window register
the runbook's licence-return step writes into the same pool and variance classification the reconciliation defines
the change log produced by executing quantity changes is the reference every invoice line is matched against
what the recurring fee buys and which revenue leg funds labour must be decided before support hours, targets and inclusions can be written
intake enforces the channel, the authorized-requester list and the severity classes that the support model defines
a request has to be classified before anyone can say whether it sits outside the fee and which of the three responses applies
the escalation decision depends on the class assigned at intake and on the ruled-out causes recorded there
the review can only inspect what the operator legitimately holds a role to inspect, and the privileged-role inventory is itself a review item
the watchlist is the between-review continuation of the findings the review established as mattering in this tenant
acting only on written instruction within a scoped authorization is the mechanism that makes every obligation-class response defensible
the watch is what usually detects the compromise, and its signals define the first artifacts the response must preserve
the review is the main manufacturer of the dated tenant-specific observations that the evidence standard requires before anything may be proposed
the catalogue may only be opened in front of a client once the evidence standard has been satisfied for that tenant
the renewal calendar is built backwards from the anniversaries and windows the term register holds
whether a churn signal should be answered with a fight or a clean handover depends on where the account sits against the measured floor
the review is the scheduled place where a detected signal becomes a conversation with evidence attached
a clean exit is the removal of exactly what the access register says the operator holds, confirmed against the same source
containment under pressure is still bounded by authorization and least privilege, and every action taken must be logged with the authority it relied on
the operator may only collect the signals its authorized roles legitimately expose, and must state honestly what the client's tier does not make visible
what may be done with a leaver's mailbox, forwarding and data is bounded by the retention, hold and monitoring classes and by written instruction
no service may be sold whose running support is not covered by the published model or explicitly priced as an addition to it
a renewal statement may carry only what is already in place plus disclosed supplier changes; an add-on needs its own evidence and its own separate acceptance
expansion is the main growth lever available to a small book while the evidence standard blocks most of the proposals that lever would produce
edges.resolution_rule: the evidence standard wins without exception: no catalogue item is presented without a dated observation in that tenant, and the revenue foregone is recorded in the recommendation log rather than argued into existence

edges.why_related: executing honest reductions lowers the account's contribution while the administrative labour that produced them stays exactly the same
edges.resolution_rule: the reduction is executed regardless and reported to the client; if the account then falls below the floor it becomes a management-fee conversation held on the measured evidence, never a reason to leave unused seats in place

edges.why_related: enforcing the boundary is exactly the behaviour most likely to produce the irritation signals that precede churn
edges.resolution_rule: name the boundary and price the work rather than absorbing it, but choose the moment deliberately and offer an alternative; if the relationship can only survive on unlimited unpaid work, let the account go cleanly rather than buying it back with silence

edges.why_related: an incident consumes hours at times the support model never covered, and the model's own boundaries argue against acting
edges.resolution_rule: contain first, because client data safety dominates the fee boundary; then bill under the stated incident clause, and if no such clause exists write one and disclose it before the next event rather than reopening the last one

edges.why_related: full disclosure of a supplier price rise arrives precisely at the moment when the client's willingness to shop around is highest
edges.resolution_rule: disclose early, separately and in writing anyway, with the supplier change and the operator's own fee on different lines; accept the churn risk rather than concealing a change the client will discover on the invoice

edges.why_related: the variances the next reconciliation finds are largely the residue of lifecycle steps that were skipped or never reported
closed findings, declined risks and enabled features are what give the account review something true to report
the tenant must be reconciled before the invoice is examined, or tenant-state variances are mistaken for billing errors and chased in the wrong place
the pre-renewal posture position must be known before the renewal statement goes out, so the term does not relock over open findings
measured minutes by class are the evidence that revises hours, severity classes, inclusions and the price the model assumes
every incident and near-miss adds a check to the review list and re-rates the severity of a finding class across the whole book

both are periodic checklist sweeps of a delivered tenant against a recorded baseline that output a dated list of differences with owners, and they share tooling, cadence and failure modes despite different subjects

conflict_axes.name: honest_true_down_vs_recurring_margin
conflict_axes.description: The reconciliation that serves the client best is the one that reduces the operator's own invoice, and no client will ever audit whether it happened.
poles: reclaim and report every unused seat
leave paid seats undisturbed and let the spread run
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reclaim regardless, report the saving to the client in the account review, and price the operator's labour in a management fee that does not move with the seat count

conflict_axes.name: evidence_led_expansion_vs_growth_pressure
conflict_axes.description: Expansion is the only growth lever a small book has that does not require new clients, and the evidence standard deliberately blocks most of it.
poles: propose only what a dated tenant observation supports
run the add-on campaign the incentive rewards
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: the tenant's evidence decides; campaigns may prompt the operator to look at a tenant but may never supply the justification, and revenue foregone is logged rather than recovered by argument

conflict_axes.name: responsiveness_vs_boundary_integrity
conflict_axes.description: The behaviour that makes a small operator loved is exactly the behaviour that makes an account unprofitable, and both effects accumulate invisibly.
poles: hold the published scope on every request
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: help deliberately and log it as a gift, or quote it, or decline and refer; never absorb silently, and let the drift ledger rather than a feeling trigger the re-pricing conversation

conflict_axes.name: least_privilege_vs_operational_speed
conflict_axes.description: Scoped, expiring, just-in-time access costs minutes on every routine job and can block the operator entirely at the moment a client is most desperate.
poles: hold the minimum role and elevate per task
keep standing rights so nothing is ever blocked
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: least privilege holds; pre-authorize an emergency elevation path with a named signer, an expiry and a log entry, so speed is designed in rather than obtained by keeping permanent rights

conflict_axes.name: commitment_term_price_vs_quantity_flexibility
conflict_axes.description: Longer commitment terms generally carry better unit economics while locking the quantity, and small businesses are the least able to predict their own headcount.
poles: commit for the longer term and take the better rate
stay short and keep the right to reduce
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: match the term to the stability of the role rather than to the whole tenant: stable core roles can carry a longer commitment while volatile, seasonal or probationary roles stay short, and the mix is documented in the term register

conflict_axes.name: signal_coverage_vs_alert_fatigue
conflict_axes.description: Every additional watch signal increases the chance of catching a compromise and increases unpaid triage time, and the operator bears the second while the client receives the first.
poles: watch only the few that are actionable
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep only signals with an owner, a written triage step and a volume the fee can actually fund; a muted signal is treated as absent and the client is told plainly what is and is not watched

conflict_axes.name: price_change_transparency_vs_retention_risk
conflict_axes.description: The most honest possible handling of a supplier price increase is also the handling most likely to start a shopping-around conversation.
poles: disclose the change early, separately and in full
let the invoice speak and hope it passes unnoticed
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: disclosure always wins; separate the supplier line from the operator's fee, give the effective date in advance, and state explicitly where the operator has chosen to absorb a change

conflict_axes.name: containment_speed_vs_evidence_preservation
conflict_axes.description: The fastest way to stop an active compromise destroys precisely the artifacts the client's insurer and advisers will later ask to see.
poles: preserve the evidence before touching anything
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: export rules, traces, sign-in and audit records to a dated store as the first containment action, then clean; where preserving would prolong active harm, contain first and record in the log exactly what was changed and when

conflict_axes.name: declined_risk_vs_continuing_to_hold_access
conflict_axes.description: A client is entitled to decline a finding, and the operator still holds administrative access to the environment that decision leaves exposed.
poles: accept the client's decision and continue
make remediation a condition of continuing to hold access
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: record the decline with date and person and restate it at every review; escalate from record to condition only where the declined item makes the operator's own duty undischargeable, and then say so plainly and offer a clean exit rather than pressure

edge_cases.description: A client asks for a departed employee's mail months after the licence was reclaimed and the recoverable window has passed
edge_cases.trigger: a reclaim executed before the client's retention decision was recorded
edge_cases.mitigation: make the written retention decision a precondition of reclaim, convert to a shared mailbox or archive per instruction, and where data is genuinely gone say so plainly and record what happened rather than implying recoverability

edge_cases.description: The client's payment method fails while their staff continue using the subscriptions the operator is still being charged for
edge_cases.trigger: a declined card or an unpaid invoice on a pass-through arrangement
edge_cases.mitigation: track collection rather than invoicing, act at the stated dunning point in the first cycle, apply the suspension policy evenly and start the conversation early rather than funding another business quietly

edge_cases.description: A supplier price revision or promotional expiry takes effect part-way through terms across several accounts at once
edge_cases.trigger: a change notice whose effective date precedes the affected anniversaries
edge_cases.mitigation: refresh the dated register, recompute affected accounts, and send written notices naming the change, its origin and its effective date with the operator's fee shown separately, before the first altered invoice arrives

edge_cases.description: The client hires a technically confident employee who asks for the tenant's global administrator credentials
edge_cases.trigger: an in-house technical hire or a new office manager taking ownership of systems
edge_cases.mitigation: treat it as the client's right rather than as a threat: provide or confirm a client-owned administrator account, re-scope the operator's roles, re-attest, and open the scope conversation early instead of defending territory

edge_cases.description: A suspected business-email compromise is reported on a Friday evening, outside every covered hour in the support model
edge_cases.trigger: an out-of-hours report of a strange sign-in prompt, a missing message or an altered payment instruction
edge_cases.mitigation: define an out-of-hours containment path in advance with an honest best-effort statement and a documented callback; contain first regardless of the clock, then bill under the stated incident clause rather than negotiating during the event

edge_cases.description: A vendor platform incident degrades mail for several clients at once and each is convinced the operator broke something
edge_cases.trigger: simultaneous unrelated reports of the same symptom across tenants
edge_cases.mitigation: check the status source before debugging, communicate on a fixed interval with what is known and unknown, never invent a restoration time, and record the event in the next account review so it is remembered accurately

edge_cases.description: The owner declines a material posture finding, such as enforcing a second factor on their own account, for the third review running
edge_cases.trigger: a repeated refusal of a high-severity remediation by the person with the authority to decide
edge_cases.mitigation: record the declined risk with date and person, restate it at each review without fear tactics or borrowed statistics, and where it makes the operator's own duty undischargeable say so plainly and offer a clean exit

edge_cases.description: The client makes staff redundant and asks to reduce seats immediately, but the current term does not permit reduction until a later date
edge_cases.trigger: a sudden headcount fall inside a committed term
edge_cases.mitigation: show the dated term entry, queue the reduction with the exact date it becomes actionable, reassign the freed licences to remaining needs in the meantime, and consider reducing the operator's own fee rather than pretending nothing can be done

edge_cases.description: A user consents to a third-party application that begins sending mail from their mailbox, or an integration breaks after a vendor change
edge_cases.trigger: an unreviewed application consent or a vendor deprecation affecting an integration
edge_cases.mitigation: keep consent review on the posture checklist and on the watchlist, classify third-party application work explicitly as billable or referred, and state the coverage boundary before the work starts rather than after

edge_cases.description: The owner asks the operator to open an employee's mailbox because they suspect wrongdoing
edge_cases.trigger: an urgent verbal request to read another person's mail
edge_cases.mitigation: require a written, scoped, dated authorization from the authorized signer, tell the client that employee-monitoring rules vary and they should verify current rules in their jurisdiction with their own adviser, log precisely what was accessed, and decline where authority or scope is unclear

edge_cases.description: A client announces they are moving to another partner and wants everything transferred by a date that suits their new provider
edge_cases.trigger: a notice of termination with a fixed handover deadline
edge_cases.mitigation: run the written exit procedure, name the program transfer mechanism and its timing consequences immediately, hand over ownership, records and documentation, confirm access removal in writing, and settle final billing as a debt question that never gates the handover

edge_cases.description: A scheduled access review finds an active administrative relationship with a client whose engagement ended a year ago
edge_cases.trigger: reconciliation of the access register against what the provider portal actually shows
edge_cases.mitigation: remove it immediately, tell the former client what was found and when it was removed, log the whole sequence, and add the missing step to the exit procedure so the gap closes rather than recurring

workflow.action: Write the recurring operating thesis and the cycle calendar
workflow.description: Fix the cadence, the unit of account, which revenue leg funds labour, and what the book explicitly does not do
workflow.artifact: operating rhythm one-pager with a cycle calendar
workflow.gate: the cadence names every recurring activity and the tenants it applies to, the labour-funding leg is stated, and at least three explicit non-offerings are listed

workflow.action: Open the per-tenant service record from the accepted handover
workflow.description: Carry the delivered documentation, subscription inventory, authorization scope, authorized requesters, escalation contacts and change log into one maintained record
workflow.gate: subscription lines, term classes, anniversaries, signer, authorized requesters, authorization scope and expiry are populated or explicitly marked unknown, and the change log is live

workflow.action: Establish access stewardship across the book
workflow.description: Scope roles to least privilege, give each person their own identity, build the access register and set the re-attestation schedule and log
workflow.artifact: access register with re-attestation schedule and privileged-action log
workflow.gate: no standing global rights without a named dated exception with an expiry, and the register reconciles to the provider portal with no unexplained relationships either way

workflow.action: Build the dated term and anniversary register
workflow.description: Record term class, billing frequency, anniversary, windows and promotional expiries per subscription, with source and date checked
workflow.gate: every live subscription line carries a term class, a billing frequency, an anniversary, a source and a checked date, and unverified rules are marked unknown rather than asserted

workflow.description: State intake, hours, severity classes and the operator's own response commitments, plus the included, billable and not-offered lists and the refusal script
workflow.gate: no sentence restates a vendor platform commitment as the operator's own, and the included, billable and not-offered lists and the authorized-requester list all exist

workflow.action: Stand up single-channel intake and triage
workflow.description: Route every request into one queue with a class, an authorization check, and captured elapsed minutes
workflow.artifact: ticket queue with classification taxonomy and time capture
workflow.gate: every request from the last cycle appears in the queue with a class, a requester, an authorization check and minutes, including those that arrived by other channels

workflow.description: Compare assigned licences, paid quantity and actual people, and classify every difference with an action and an owner
workflow.gate: all three counts are present with sources, every difference is classified, and the client-favouring classes are reported to the client whether or not they reduce the invoice

workflow.description: Provision additions, execute permitted reductions, queue blocked ones with their actionable dates, and verify every change
workflow.gate: each change has a written request, an effective date and a verification result, each blocked reduction has its actionable date, and no reclaim precedes a recorded retention decision

workflow.action: Reconcile the provider invoice, the tenant and the client invoice
workflow.description: Match lines against the change log, explain every variance, confirm collection and apply the stated dunning position
workflow.artifact: reconciled invoice pack with variance explanations
workflow.gate: every provider line is matched or explained, realised spread is computed from actual charges, and collection status is known for every account

workflow.action: Run the security posture review and set the drift watchlist
workflow.description: Work the checklist against the delivered baseline, produce findings with severity, fix, owner and date, record declines, and tune the between-review signals
workflow.artifact: dated findings list and tuned watchlist
workflow.gate: every checklist item is answered or marked unknown, every finding and decline is attributed and dated, and each enabled signal has an owner, a triage step and an expected volume

workflow.action: Run the renewal and repricing cycle
workflow.description: Work backwards from each anniversary, reconcile before the term relocks, and send the written renewal statement with supplier changes separated from the operator's fee
workflow.artifact: renewal calendar and written renewal statements
workflow.gate: each statement went out before its notice window closed, names quantity, term, price, date and what can still be changed, and carries no add-on that was not separately accepted

workflow.action: Hold the account review and decide the account's future
workflow.description: Present the one-page record of work, posture, administration and recommendations, review the drift ledger and measured cost, and decide to continue, re-price, re-scope or exit
workflow.artifact: one-page account review with a recorded account decision
workflow.gate: every figure traces to the operator's own records, declined risks and non-coverage are restated, and any below-floor account carries a written decision with a date

priority_rationale: The frame units come first because the operating rhythm and the per-tenant service record decide whether any later cycle can be executed at all, and access stewardship comes immediately after because every other unit acts inside someone else's tenant under that authority. The licence-administration units follow because the term register governs what may be said about any seat and the reconciliation supplies the facts the invoice is checked against. The support units come next because they bound what the fee buys before any measurement of cost is meaningful. The recurring-value units then convert access and rhythm into the posture evidence that later justifies both the fee and any recommendation. The expansion, renewal and retention units come last because each consumes evidence the earlier units produce, and the exit unit is written first but executed last, because how the operator leaves is decided long before anyone leaves.

dominance_rules.rule: Documented authorization and least privilege dominate speed, convenience and client urgency inside a live tenant
dominance_rules.rationale: administrative access to a small business's mail and identity plane is held on that client's behalf, and urgency never changes what an unauthorized action is
dominance_rules.trigger: any request to act in a tenant without a current written authorization covering that class of action, or any proposal to keep standing rights for convenience
dominance_rules.action: pause, obtain a scoped authorization from the named signer, record it, and only then act

dominance_rules.rule: Client data safety dominates the fee boundary during an active incident
dominance_rules.rationale: an unbounded support argument is recoverable while a compromise left running is not
dominance_rules.trigger: a suspected compromise arrives outside covered hours or beyond what the fee includes
dominance_rules.action: contain and preserve evidence first, then settle the commercial question under the stated incident clause afterwards

dominance_rules.rule: A dated tenant-specific observation dominates every expansion opportunity
dominance_rules.rationale: the operator is the only party able to evaluate its own recommendation, and a recommendation bent toward the spread destroys the position the whole business rests on
dominance_rules.trigger: an add-on, tier or seat looks commercially attractive without a dated observation in that tenant
dominance_rules.action: do not propose it; record the opportunity and the reason it was not raised, and revisit only if evidence appears

dominance_rules.rule: Evidence preservation dominates cleanup speed once a compromise is suspected
dominance_rules.rationale: rules, traces and audit records age out of retention and are exactly what a client's insurer or adviser will ask for months later
dominance_rules.trigger: the first containment action is about to modify or delete attacker artifacts
dominance_rules.action: export the artifacts to a dated store first, unless preserving would prolong active harm, in which case contain and log precisely what was changed

dominance_rules.rule: The dated term register dominates memory in every seat and price conversation
dominance_rules.rationale: program terms are vendor-controlled and revised without the operator noticing, and a confident wrong answer becomes a promise
dominance_rules.trigger: any statement about what can be added, reduced, cancelled or re-priced and by when
dominance_rules.action: answer from the register with its checked date, or say it must be verified and then verify it

dominance_rules.rule: Honest true-down dominates the operator's own recurring revenue
dominance_rules.rationale: the reconciliation exists to serve the client, and a reconciliation that only ever adds seats will eventually be recognised for what it is
dominance_rules.trigger: the variance list shows paid seats with no user
dominance_rules.action: execute or queue the reduction and report it to the client, then treat any resulting economics as a management-fee conversation

dominance_rules.rule: Disclosure dominates smoothness whenever a price or term changes
dominance_rules.rationale: a client who discovers a change on an invoice learns that the operator preferred not to tell them
dominance_rules.trigger: a supplier price revision, a promotional expiry, or any change to what the client pays
dominance_rules.action: state the change, its origin and its effective date in writing before it takes effect, with the operator's own fee on a separate line

dominance_rules.rule: The client's ownership of their tenant and data dominates the operator's commercial position at every exit
dominance_rules.rationale: withholding access converts a fiduciary position into leverage and destroys the only asset a small operator really has
dominance_rules.trigger: an exit occurs with an unpaid invoice, a dispute, or a competitor taking over
dominance_rules.action: hand over ownership, records and documentation, remove access and confirm it in writing, and pursue any debt entirely separately

dominance_rules.rule: A written boundary dominates silent absorption of out-of-scope work
dominance_rules.rationale: absorbed work earns no goodwill because nobody knows it happened, and it destroys the account's economics invisibly
dominance_rules.trigger: a request arrives that the published model does not include
dominance_rules.action: gift it and log it, quote it, or decline and refer, and record the minutes either way

dominance_rules.rule: Named obligation classes and written instruction dominate improvised advice
dominance_rules.rationale: a small reseller is not qualified to interpret data-protection, employment or notification law, and a helpful sentence can become a liability for both parties
dominance_rules.trigger: a retention, export, monitoring, notification or jurisdiction question arrives
dominance_rules.action: name the class, require written instruction, preserve rather than delete while unclear, and refer the client to their own adviser and to current rules in their jurisdiction

anti_rework_rules.rule: Record the client's written retention decision for a departing person's mailbox and data before reclaiming the licence
anti_rework_rules.prevents: irreversible loss of data the client needed, discovered months later when no recovery path remains

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the dated term and anniversary register before promising any addition, reduction, cancellation or renewal price
anti_rework_rules.prevents: promises the program does not permit, and reissued statements and apologies after the provider says no

anti_rework_rules.rule: Publish the support model and the single intake channel before accepting the first ticket on a new account
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unbounded relationship that has to be renegotiated after the client has already learned different habits

anti_rework_rules.rule: Reconcile the tenant's assigned licences against the change log before examining the provider invoice
anti_rework_rules.prevents: hours spent chasing billing variances that are really tenant-state variances, and credits requested for changes the operator itself made

anti_rework_rules.rule: Capture minutes per ticket and per administrative cycle from the first month rather than reconstructing them when a re-price is needed
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a re-pricing conversation with no evidence, which the client can refuse and which damages the relationship for nothing

anti_rework_rules.rule: Re-attest delegated access on a schedule and at every staffing or signer change on either side
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering stale or excessive access during an incident or a review, when it is indefensible and cannot be explained away

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the seat reconciliation and the posture review before issuing any renewal statement
anti_rework_rules.prevents: relocking a term on the wrong quantity and over open findings, which cannot be undone until the next window

anti_rework_rules.rule: Establish and date the tenant-specific evidence line before an add-on is mentioned to the client at all
anti_rework_rules.prevents: retro-fitting a justification onto a recommendation already made, which reads as selling and cannot be defended when questioned

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pass the capability test, including an actual timed restore or an actually authored policy, before offering the service that depends on it
anti_rework_rules.prevents: discovering during a real client emergency that the operator cannot deliver what it sold

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the exit procedure and show it to the client at the start of the relationship
anti_rework_rules.prevents: improvising an offboarding under time pressure and leaving credentials, delegated access or unreturned documentation behind

iteration_protocol.trigger: a supplier price revision, promotional expiry or term restructure is announced
iteration_protocol.action: refresh the dated term register, recompute affected accounts, and issue written notices with origin and effective date before the first altered invoice

iteration_protocol.trigger: a full cycle of measured minutes shows an account sitting below the cost-to-serve floor
iteration_protocol.action: decide explicitly between re-pricing, re-scoping and a clean exit, using the drift ledger and the measured contribution as the evidence, and record the decision with a date

iteration_protocol.trigger: an incident or near-miss occurs in any tenant in the book
iteration_protocol.action: add the missed check to the posture checklist, re-rate the related finding severity, re-run that check across every tenant, and revise the response procedure where it fell short

iteration_protocol.trigger: the vendor changes its delegated-administration model, admin role catalogue or expiry behaviour
iteration_protocol.action: re-map every tenant's roles to least privilege, re-attest the whole register, update the service records, and note the dated change in the register

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same ticket class recurs across several accounts within one cycle
iteration_protocol.action: treat it as a cause rather than a coincidence: fix the standard, the runbook step or the client-side habit once, and update the support model if the class turns out to be structurally mis-scoped

iteration_protocol.trigger: a churn signal fires on an account
iteration_protocol.action: open the conversation before the renewal window rather than during it, refresh the value evidence, and decide honestly whether to work for the account or offer a clean handover

iteration_protocol.trigger: a client declines the same material posture finding for a third review
iteration_protocol.action: record the accepted risk with date and person, restate the operator's position in writing without pressure tactics, and decide whether continuing to hold administrative access remains defensible

iteration_protocol.trigger: an expansion proposal is declined, or a sold add-on proves unsupportable in practice
iteration_protocol.action: record the reason rather than re-pitching, and either retire the item from the catalogue, re-scope it, or price the operating labour it actually turned out to need
